title: Welded Fields
description: Stigmergic trail crossed with procedural advection on one shared grid.

cogdoc.claim: A stigmergic system can close its own loop: with the exogenous noise gain at zero the transport field is entirely agent-deposited and the governing quantity is an internal ratio of timescales (momentum half-life / trail half-life). Measuring that system requires normalization robust to deposit spikes (99.5th percentile, not raw max) and a threshold that fixes mask COVERAGE rather than LEVEL, which is what makes beta_1 comparable across parameter changes.

changes: head, after <title>: added an embedded <script type="application/cogdoc+yaml"> frontmatter block carrying the canonical cogdoc core (id `paper-welded-fields`, type `paper`, title, description, sector, status, created, updated, salience, authors, tags) plus the paper-conditional fields required by .cog/conf/spec/cogdoc-html-executable-artifacts.cog.md: `claim`, `method[]` with one entry per free parameter (all 18 sidebar sliders plus fixed N=9000, each with range, default, unit where applicable, and a MEANING — a parameter with no stated meaning is a knob, not a method), `observables` naming window.__sim and the cost of each call, `findings[]`, `limitations[]`, and typed `refs[]`. WHY: the artifact previously asserted its corrections in code comments only — line 265's 'reallocated with the grid, unlike the original' and line 625's coverage-vs-level note were unaddressable and uncountable. Spec rule 5 requires any 'unlike the original'-class comment to become a typed ref, so the physarum correction is now `refs[] uri:app:physarum rel:corrects` and is queryable as a graph edge rather than folklore. The block is inert to the renderer (scripts of unknown type are neither executed nor rendered), so the file is simultaneously a running artifact and an indexable cogdoc. Declared here because this app is kind `frozen-golden` and spec rule 3 makes any edit to a frozen-golden entry a declared change with its reason. Verified after the edit: cogdoc_html.py validate -> OK [paper] paper-welded-fields with zero errors and zero warnings; headless Chromium load via cogdoc_verify.py -> canvas non-zero, lit pixels non-zero, zero console errors, and __sim.betti()/refs() checked against the stated findings.

topology census made periodic (issue #38). euler() and components() (the `topology` block before measure()) read the mask as a zero-padded flat square (bit-quads over x,y in [-1,W) x [-1,H) with out-of-range cells = 0; flood fill skipped out-of-range neighbours) while the agents, trail diffusion and momentum field all wrap on a torus. Fixed: bit-quads now run over x,y in [0,W) x [0,H) with indices taken mod W,H, the 8-neighbour flood fill wraps mod W,H, and measure() and __sim.betti() use the torus relation chi = b0 - b1 + b2, i.e. b1 = b0 + b2 - euler() with b2 = 1 only when the mask covers every cell. Cogdoc observables.betti, limitations[0] and the panel note restated to match; no dynamics, parameter or default changed. Verified by driving analytic masks through the page's own measure() on the real page (605x400; torus answer / before / after, as b0,b1): empty 0,0 / 0,0 / 0,0; disk in the interior 1,0 / 1,0 / 1,0; disk centred on the corner seam 1,0 / 4,0 / 1,0; full-width band 1,1 / 1,0 / 1,1; ring crossing the x-seam 1,1 / 2,0 / 1,1; full-width + full-height cross 1,2 / 1,0 / 1,2; full mask 1,2 / 1,0 / 1,2. EFFECT ON THE HEADLINE OBSERVABLE, stated plainly: at the defaults (thr = 8% coverage) the census read the same before and after on all 5 seeds tested at 1500 frames (seeded run, before (b0,b1) = after (b0,b1) = s1 2,1; s2 2,0; s3 1,2; s4 3,0; s5 2,1) and at 2400 frames, because the swarm is seeded in a central disk and at 8% coverage the mask had no cell pair across the seam in any of those runs. The flat census only diverges once the mask touches the seam: at 20% and 40% coverage after 2400 frames, seed 1 (82 seam pairs) and seed 5 (26 seam pairs) read b0 = 2 flat vs 1 on the torus (b1 unchanged in those cases). So the paper's coverage-invariance finding is not overturned by this fix at its defaults, but b1 values measured earlier at high coverage or on long runs were counts on the square, not the torus, and are not comparable with values from this version.
